Let \(a_n=a_1+f(n)\). Then naturally
- \(a_{n+1}=a_1+f(n+1)\) (so <missing 1> is expression 1),
- \(a_{n+k}=a_1+f(n+k)\) (so <missing 2> is expression 10).

Define the product condition via an offset function \(g(j)\):
- \(P=\prod_{j=1}^k a_{n+j}=\prod_{j=1}^k (a_n+g(j))\) (so <missing 3> is expression 13).

“Coefficients of <missing 4> to be positive” refers to coefficients of \(P(a_n)\) as a polynomial in \(a_n\), so <missing 4> is \(P(a_n)\) (expression 7). To keep coefficients nonnegative we need \(g(j)\ge 0\) for all \(j\) (expression 22), and then the expansion is
- \(P=a_n^k+C_{k-1}a_n^{k-1}+\cdots +C_1 a_n+\prod_{j=1}^k g(j)=P(a_n)\) (expression 18).

Next, matching terms requires
- \(a_n+g(j)=a_{n+j}=a_1+f(n+j)\) (expression 14),
so
- \(g(j)=f(n+j)-f(n)\) (expression 8),
and nonnegativity gives
- \(g(j)=f(n+j)-f(n)\ge 0\) (expression 11).

Also \(f(1)=0\) because \(a_1=a_1+f(1)\) (expression 16).

For independence of \(n\), they refer to the form
- \(g(j)=a_1+f(n+j)-a_n=a_1+f(n+j)-a_1-f(n)\) (expression 20),
so the \(n\)-dependence must cancel, forcing \(f\) linear:
- \(f(n)=mn+b\) (expression 15), with intercept at \(n=0\) (expression 9).
Since \(f(1)=0\), \(m+b=0\) (expression 4), hence \(b=-m\) (expression 21), so
- \(f(n)=mn-m=(n-1)m\) (expression 19).
Nonnegativity/integrality forces \(m\ge 0,\, m\in\mathbb Z\) (expression 3).

Then
- \(g(j)=f(n+j)-f(n)=jm\) (expression 6),
so
- \(\prod_{j=1}^k (a_n+jm)=P(a_n)=a_n^k+C_{k-1}a_n^{k-1}+\cdots+C_1a_n+k!m^k\) (expression 2),
with constant term \(C_0=k!m^k\) (expression 5); and the coefficients are those of \(P(a_n)\) (expression 7).

Finally \(a_n=a_1+f(n)=a_1+(n-1)m\) (expression 24), with \(a_1\ge 1, a_1\in\mathbb Z\) (expression 12) and \(m\ge 0, m\in\mathbb Z\) (expression 23).

Answer: 1, 10, 13, 7, 22, 18, 14, 8, 11, 16, 20, 15, 9, 4, 21, 19, 3, 6, 2, 5, 7, 24, 12, 23
